title: Messiah
author: handel
attributionNote: Recorded in the Christian Classics Ethereal Library under George Frideric Handel (1685-1759). The site catalogues the work at https://ccel.org/ccel/handel/messiah, whose own card names the print edition transcribed here; where the site carries a title by a publisher's permission rather than in public domain, this library does not take it.
description: Messiah — the English text the Christian Classics Ethereal Library publishes for this work, on the site's Hymns shelf. The record was created by the CCEL import from the site's own catalogue and plain text; an editor's note for the work itself is still to be written.
historicalContext: Read in the Christian Classics Ethereal Library's catalogue, whose shelves follow the site's own division of Christian literature, and whose transcription follows the print edition New York: G. Schirmer, 1912.
availabilityNote: Complete in the Christian Classics Ethereal Library's plain-text edition: 1 chapter(s), 53 paragraph(s), 380 words. The divisions are the headings of the site's own text, which the library stores rather than asking the site for again when the work is read. The text is public domain and is displayed with the library's credit.

editions.title: Messiah

texts.1.6: 6. But who may abide the day of his coming?
texts.1.9: 9. O thou that tellest good tidings to Zion
texts.1.10: 10. For, behold, darkness shall cover the earth
texts.1.11: 11. The people that walked in darkness
texts.1.12: 12. For unto us a child is born

texts.1.15: 15. And the angel said unto them
texts.1.16: 16. And suddenly there was with the angel
texts.1.18: 18. Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion
texts.1.19: 19. Then shall the eyes of the blind be opened
texts.1.20: 20. He shall feed his flock like a shepherd
texts.1.21: 21. His yoke is easy and his burthen is light
texts.1.24: 24. Surely He hath borne our griefs
texts.1.25: 25. And with His stripes we are healed
texts.1.26: 26. All we like sheep have gone astray
texts.1.27: 27. All they that see Him, laugh him to scorn
texts.1.28: 28. He trusted in God that He would deliver Him
texts.1.29: 29. Thy rebuke hath broken his heart
texts.1.30: 30. Behold and see if there be any sorrow

texts.1.36: 36. Thou art gone up on high
texts.1.38: 38. How beautiful are the feet of them
texts.1.39: 39. Their sound has gone out into all the lands
texts.1.40: 40. Why do the nations so furiously rage
texts.1.41: 41. Let us break their bonds asunder
texts.1.45: 45. I know that my Redeemer liveth
